subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned session authentication gate, or should this remain a plugin/API-extension pattern built on `before_tool_call`?
rationale: The request crosses config shape, secret handling, session state, reset semantics, transcript redaction, and fail-closed tool execution, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary or default behavior.

options.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
options.body: Add a core primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, compatibility, and recovery UX.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Treat the current hook surface as the enforcement seam and document or extend plugin APIs so deployments can opt into session gates outside core.

options.title: Defer the PIN gate
options.body: Leave existing sandboxing, approvals, allowlists, and external-content wrapping as the supported mitigation until a stronger step-up-auth design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
recommendation.body: Add a core primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, compatibility, and recovery UX.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the implicated session/tool/config files and is already in the issue timeline context for this product/security decision.
